Because a leaking lower tank saturates its own loop at 12 V, this threshold catches sustained/severe leaks but misses the milder leak phases where effort settles between roughly 9.5 and 11.4 V (tank1_leak t1=91 missed, tank2_leak phase around t=280-330 t2 missed). It also has no hysteresis on the flag, so as soon as the effort dips one call below 11.5 V the flag drops off while the fault persists (both_leaks t1 missed from t=260), and it has no positive leak evidence other than extreme effort. Meanwhile the setpoint reduction gradually pulls the tank down, which lowers the demand and the effort, so the supervisor's own mitigation erases the very signal it uses to detect the leak, causing the flag to fall and the fault to be missed. Conversely, the restore path keys on 'eff1_low and sp1 < nom1', and after a mitigation the effort is genuinely low, so setpoints are stepped back toward nominal while the fault is still active, producing the flip-flop and residual restore_gap (0.04-0.18 m). No false positive on baseline because the healthy settled effort ranges (tank1 8.79-10.54 V, tank2 8.52-9.26 V) never reach 11.5 V; but the pure-threshold detector also produces false positives on the OTHER tank after one tank's leak clears, when effort momentarily exceeds 11.5 V during the recovery transient (tank2_leak t1 false_pos=50 around t=490-540, when tank1 effort rose to 11.5 V as tank2 recovered).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single fixed effort threshold with per-tank, level-relative leak evidence that combines (a) loop effort above a per-tank elevated band that is high relative to healthy mean and trending/sustained, and (b) the tank level sitting below its active setpoint despite the elevated effort, so a genuine leak remains detectable through setpoint mitigation. Add an asymmetry so that elevated effort in one loop is attributed to that loop's tank only when that loop's own level error is also elevated, preventing cross-loop false positives during the other tank's recovery transient. Use hysteresis counters (enter on K consecutive calls, exit only after several consecutive clear calls) for both flags and gate setpoint restoration on the flag being cleared plus effort returning near the healthy mean, so setpoints are not restored while a fault is still active.
relations_learned: A mitigated setpoint lowers pump demand, so effort-alone detectors lose the leak signal; detection must use level-versus-setpoint error.
Effort in one loop spikes above healthy mean during the other tank's fault recovery, so per-loop flags need own-loop level evidence.

Start-up healthy mean|error| tank1=0.1262 (range 0.0743-0.1558), tank2=0.1091 (range 0.0499-0.1531); effort tank1 range [4.15, 10.59] V, tank2 [6.08, 8.76] V. My entry condition for tank1 requires BOTH mean effort over the last 5 samples > 10.6 V (above healthy settled max 10.54 V by 0.06 V, so healthy can barely reach it; start-up max 10.59 V excluded by requiring the level below setpoint AND requiring 3 consecutive calls) AND current error (setpoint - level) > 0.07 m (above healthy settled max 0.0736 m only marginally, and above mean|e| 0.0154 by 4.5x; start-up mean|e| up to 0.1558 is excluded because during start-up the level is below setpoint for a reason and effort is only briefly high, so the 3-call streak plus the 10.6 V effort gate rejects it: during start-up tank1 effort is below 10.6 V for most rows). For tank2 I require mean effort > 9.5 V (above healthy settled max 9.26 V by 0.24 V) AND error > 0.075 m (above healthy settled max 0.0495 m by 1.5x; start-up tank2 mean|e| up to 0.1531 m is rejected because tank2 effort during start-up never exceeds 8.76 V, below the 9.5 V gate). Exit requires 4 consecutive calls with effort below 10.2 V (tank1) / 9.2 V (tank2) AND error below 0.06 m, so the flag is sticky and does not chatter on one noisy sample; the 0.06 m exit threshold is above the healthy settled error maxima (0.0736 tank1, 0.0495 tank2) only for tank2, so tank1 exit also needs the effort to fall back below 10.2 V (healthy settled mean 9.35 V) which is the stronger signal. All gates are above the respective healthy settled effort maxima, giving zero false positives on the fault-free settled reference.
proposed_change: Replace the single fixed effort threshold with a per-tank sticky leak detector combining sustained elevated loop effort (tank1 > ~10.6 V, tank2 > ~9.5 V over the last 5 samples) with own-loop level error above a healthy-settled maximum (tank1 > 0.07 m, tank2 > 0.075 m), entering after 3 consecutive calls and clearing only after 4 consecutive clear calls, so effort dips caused by the supervisor's own setpoint mitigation do not drop the flag. Restore a tank's setpoint toward nominal only when its flag is clear and its effort has returned to the healthy band, and step setpoints down more slowly (0.015 m) to keep the mitigation from hiding the fault while reducing restore_gap.
